newsitem.title: USA: Calif. court ruling may hit $480 mln road projects.
newsitem.headline: Calif. court ruling may hit $480 mln road projects.

text.p: California transportation officials warned Friday the state Supreme Court's decision to limit contracting could force delays to $480 million of road projects and scuttle contracts worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
"The projects will still get done, but there could be delays," said California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) spokesman Jim Drago. "We're still trying to sort out where we go from here."
Thursday, California's Supreme Court upheld decades-old restrictions barring state agencies from hiring private contractors to perform work that can be done as well and as cheaply by state employees.
The court ruled that Caltrans is bound by court precedents limiting the state's authority to contract with private entities to perform services the state has "historically or customarily" performed.
"The civil service mandate forbids private contracts for work that the state itself can perform 'adequately and competently,'" the court's majority said in its ruling.
The state Supreme Court decision stemmed from a 1986 lawsuit by a labor group representing state engineers.
The group asked the courts to bar Caltrans from contracting with private entities for state highway projects, work traditionally done by state civil service employees.
Loren McMaster, an attorney for the group, said the ruling was a "tremendous victory" for state workers, and a set back for California Gov. Pete Wilson's privatization efforts.
